title: pcell: the within-cell yield decline is absolute, not just a rank effect, and it happens even with no explicit replication cost
summary: Follow-up to 20261025T0923-c06-pcell-somatic-decline. Rank declines could arise only because the population improves around a constant cell, so abslife.py compares each dying mature cell's absolute mean yield at birth and at death with the population mean at the same times. With cost cy=0.03 (3 seeds at muy 0.02, 2 at muy 0.002), dying cells fall from 0.93-0.98 to 0.66-0.81 while the population mean stays at 0.93-1.05; 77-100% of them declined. With no explicit cost (cy=0, 2 seeds) they still fall, from 1.07 to 0.98, while the population rises from 1.08-1.10 to 1.19-1.21 (64-86% declined). Low yield is therefore favoured inside a cell even without the explicit cost, plausibly because a particle's link production b y S m draws on the substrate S at its own position, which its own duplication rate c S (1-K) also needs (a hidden local cost; not separately ablated). Cells in this world age by within-cell erosion of the public good at any cost value tested.

finding.operator: particle-level public-good link yield inside self-made cells
finding.control: population mean yield at the same times (abslife.txt); cy=0 arm
